title: Angelia event envelope, v1 (draft, pre-1.0)
description: Angelia's profile of a CloudEvents 1.0 event in JSON structured mode. The set of event types is open: type is any dev.angelia.<short type>.v<major> name, and new types can appear in a minor release of the spec. Consumers must ignore events whose type they do not know. The release event types dev.angelia.release.published.v1, dev.angelia.release.yanked.v1 and dev.angelia.release.prerelease.v1 share one data schema (schemas/release/v1.json); for them, subject and dataschema follow the release rules (one allOf if/then entry per type), and data, like that of any event whose dataschema names schemas/release/v1.json, must validate against it (one allOf if/then entry keyed on dataschema). This is the single v1 envelope of every event type: a new type adds its own if/then entries to allOf (its subject and dataschema rules, and the data rule of its data schema), which narrows only events of a type nobody emitted before, so it is an additive change. For a type with no entry, subject is a non-empty string, dataschema the URI of that type's data schema, and data is not checked by this schema. DRAFT: while the spec repository is at version 0.x this profile may still change in a breaking way in any 0.x minor release; it is frozen at spec 1.0.0. v1 defines no extension attributes and producers emit none, but other producers or intermediaries (brokers, tracing) may add CloudEvents extension attributes: any attribute whose name is 1 to 20 lower-case letters or digits is allowed, and consumers must ignore attributes they do not know. Other unknown names are rejected.

type.description: Event type: reverse-DNS prefix dev.angelia., the short type, then .v<major>. The short type (for example release.published) is the type without the dev.angelia. prefix and the .v<major> suffix; it is what subscription filters use. Each dot-separated segment is non-empty. An open set: today's types are dev.angelia.release.published.v1, dev.angelia.release.yanked.v1 and dev.angelia.release.prerelease.v1; adding a type is a minor (additive) change. Consumers must ignore events whose type they do not know.

source.description: The watch that produced the event: angelia://<instance>/watches/<watch_id>, where <instance> is the instance name from the instance configuration and <watch_id> equals data.watch.id.

id.description: Event id: a ULID (26 characters, Crockford base32, upper case) generated once when the event is written. Every delivery attempt, retry and replay of the event carries the same id; consumers deduplicate on it. source + id is globally unique.

subject.description: Identifies what the event is about, so brokers and routers can filter without parsing data. The form depends on the type: for the release types, <source kind>:<package>@<version> with the raw upstream version (data.source, data.package, data.version); for another type, as that type's documentation says.

time.description: When the event was emitted (the end of the check that emitted it): RFC 3339, UTC, Z suffix, at most millisecond precision. With a cooldown this is later than data.detected_at.

dataschema.description: URI of the data schema of the event's type: for the release types, the $id of schemas/release/v1.json. An identifier, not promised to be fetchable.

data.description: The event payload, described by the data schema of the event's type: for the release types, schemas/release/v1.json.

allOf.$comment: data is checked against the release data schema whenever dataschema names it, so every release type (whose dataschema is that const) has its data checked. Keyed on dataschema rather than repeated in each type's then: the release data schema is referenced once, so bundlers that inline external schemas (Spectral) do not get its $id twice. A new type with its own data schema adds one such entry for that schema.
